method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Kishnani PS, Austin SL, Abdenur JE, et al., Genetics in Medicine (ACMG) 'Diagnosis and management of glycogen storage disease type I: a practice guideline of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics' (vol. 16, e1, published 2014). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: © American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (free to read; no open licence) (read at the '© American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics' line on the first page of the publisher PDF (nature.com/articles/gim2014128.pdf, free to read; Unpaywall: bronze, no licence)). The source's words are NOT reproduced here. Text extracted with pdftotext in reading order (not -layout). Only running text and the guideline's summary recommendation boxes were anchored; the food and mutation tables were not.

claims.claim: **Low glucose, lactic acidosis, raised cholesterol and triglycerides, and high uric acid together fit GSD I;** neutropenia points to type Ib, though it can occur in Ia and may be absent in Ib in early childhood.
claims.locator: Kishnani PS, Austin SL, Abdenur JE, et al., Genetics in Medicine (ACMG), 'Diagnosis and management of glycogen storage disease type I: a practice guideline of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics', vol. 16, e1, published 2014, https://doi.org/10.1038/gim.2014.128, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Confirm by sequencing G6PC (Ia) and SLC37A4 (Ib);** liver biopsy is not needed when GSD is suspected, now that gene testing is available.
claims.locator: Kishnani PS, Austin SL, Abdenur JE, et al., Genetics in Medicine (ACMG), 'Diagnosis and management of glycogen storage disease type I: a practice guideline of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics', vol. 16, e1, published 2014, https://doi.org/10.1038/gim.2014.128, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Undiagnosed or undertreated children can drop below 40 mg/dl after only 3–4 hours of fasting;** prolonged hypoglycaemia risks developmental delay, seizures, brain damage and death.
claims.locator: Kishnani PS, Austin SL, Abdenur JE, et al., Genetics in Medicine (ACMG), 'Diagnosis and management of glycogen storage disease type I: a practice guideline of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics', vol. 16, e1, published 2014, https://doi.org/10.1038/gim.2014.128, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoiding fasting is the first-line treatment:** small, frequent feeds rich in complex carbohydrate spread over 24 hours, aiming for blood glucose of at least 70 mg/dl without big swings.
claims.locator: Kishnani PS, Austin SL, Abdenur JE, et al., Genetics in Medicine (ACMG), 'Diagnosis and management of glycogen storage disease type I: a practice guideline of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics', vol. 16, e1, published 2014, https://doi.org/10.1038/gim.2014.128, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Diet mix:** 60–70% of calories from carbohydrate, 10–15% from protein, and fat below 30% after age 2; sucrose, fructose and lactose are usually limited, so a complete multivitamin with minerals, plus calcium and vitamin D, is essential.
claims.locator: Kishnani PS, Austin SL, Abdenur JE, et al., Genetics in Medicine (ACMG), 'Diagnosis and management of glycogen storage disease type I: a practice guideline of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics', vol. 16, e1, published 2014, https://doi.org/10.1038/gim.2014.128, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Infants:** sucrose-, fructose- and lactose-free (or soy) formula on demand every 2–3 hours; once sleeping longer, either wake to feed or use overnight gastric feeds. Parents should be trained to pass an NG tube, or a gastrostomy placed, so glucose can always be given.
claims.locator: Kishnani PS, Austin SL, Abdenur JE, et al., Genetics in Medicine (ACMG), 'Diagnosis and management of glycogen storage disease type I: a practice guideline of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics', vol. 16, e1, published 2014, https://doi.org/10.1038/gim.2014.128, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **In GSD Ib with neutropenia, a gastrostomy carries infection risk** and should only be placed if G-CSF is being given.
claims.locator: Kishnani PS, Austin SL, Abdenur JE, et al., Genetics in Medicine (ACMG), 'Diagnosis and management of glycogen storage disease type I: a practice guideline of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics', vol. 16, e1, published 2014, https://doi.org/10.1038/gim.2014.128, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Overnight tube feeds usually deliver glucose at 8–10 mg glucose/kg/min in infancy and 4–8 in older children;** feed straight after stopping them, and use pump alarms and other safety measures because pump failure has caused deaths.
claims.locator: Kishnani PS, Austin SL, Abdenur JE, et al., Genetics in Medicine (ACMG), 'Diagnosis and management of glycogen storage disease type I: a practice guideline of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics', vol. 16, e1, published 2014, https://doi.org/10.1038/gim.2014.128, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Raw uncooked cornstarch is usually trialled between 6 months and 1 year;** a guide is 1.6 g/kg every 3–4 hours in young children and 1.7–2.5 g/kg every 4–5 hours (sometimes 6) in older children and adults. Increase from a small starting dose for tolerance.
claims.locator: Kishnani PS, Austin SL, Abdenur JE, et al., Genetics in Medicine (ACMG), 'Diagnosis and management of glycogen storage disease type I: a practice guideline of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics', vol. 16, e1, published 2014, https://doi.org/10.1038/gim.2014.128, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Modified cornstarch (Glycosade) can be used overnight,** but only with close monitoring of metabolic control; any change of cornstarch brand or dose should be supervised by the metabolic team with frequent glucose checks. Do not mix cornstarch with hot water, lemonade or high-dose vitamin C.
claims.locator: Kishnani PS, Austin SL, Abdenur JE, et al., Genetics in Medicine (ACMG), 'Diagnosis and management of glycogen storage disease type I: a practice guideline of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics', vol. 16, e1, published 2014, https://doi.org/10.1038/gim.2014.128, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Adolescents and adults:** avoid fasting beyond 5–6 hours with cornstarch and/or overnight feeds, and keep checking glucose and lactate even when feeling well. Overtreatment is harmful too, causing insulin resistance.
claims.locator: Kishnani PS, Austin SL, Abdenur JE, et al., Genetics in Medicine (ACMG), 'Diagnosis and management of glycogen storage disease type I: a practice guideline of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics', vol. 16, e1, published 2014, https://doi.org/10.1038/gim.2014.128, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Treat glucose below 60 mg/dl with fast-acting glucose, then a snack or cornstarch to hold it.** Patients may feel nothing until levels are very low. Everyone should wear a medical alert bracelet.
claims.locator: Kishnani PS, Austin SL, Abdenur JE, et al., Genetics in Medicine (ACMG), 'Diagnosis and management of glycogen storage disease type I: a practice guideline of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics', vol. 16, e1, published 2014, https://doi.org/10.1038/gim.2014.128, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Surgery:** admit 24 h beforehand for IV D10; **never use lactated Ringer's** (worsens lactic acidosis); do not stop IV glucose abruptly, only once the patient is eating and holding glucose.
claims.locator: Kishnani PS, Austin SL, Abdenur JE, et al., Genetics in Medicine (ACMG), 'Diagnosis and management of glycogen storage disease type I: a practice guideline of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics', vol. 16, e1, published 2014, https://doi.org/10.1038/gim.2014.128, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Liver:** image the abdomen at baseline and every 12–24 months (ultrasound in children), moving to CT/MRI with contrast every 6–12 months once adenomas appear. A rapid rise in adenoma size or number raises concern for cancer; alpha-fetoprotein does not predict it.
claims.locator: Kishnani PS, Austin SL, Abdenur JE, et al., Genetics in Medicine (ACMG), 'Diagnosis and management of glycogen storage disease type I: a practice guideline of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics', vol. 16, e1, published 2014, https://doi.org/10.1038/gim.2014.128, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Kidney:** at routine visits check renal ultrasound, urinalysis, urine albumin, citrate and calcium, and electrolytes with eGFR. Microalbuminuria that persists (>30 μg albumin /mg creatinine) or overt proteinuria calls for ACE-inhibitor or ARB treatment; consider it for hyperfiltration too (eGFR >140). Give citrate for low urinary citrate.
claims.locator: Kishnani PS, Austin SL, Abdenur JE, et al., Genetics in Medicine (ACMG), 'Diagnosis and management of glycogen storage disease type I: a practice guideline of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics', vol. 16, e1, published 2014, https://doi.org/10.1038/gim.2014.128, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Blood:** investigate anaemia (diet, adenomas, enterocolitis, menorrhagia, occult loss). In GSD Ib, treat neutropenia with the lowest effective G-CSF dose, beginning with 0.5–1.0 µg/kg/day by subcutaneous injection, especially with recurrent fever, infections or enterocolitis.
claims.locator: Kishnani PS, Austin SL, Abdenur JE, et al., Genetics in Medicine (ACMG), 'Diagnosis and management of glycogen storage disease type I: a practice guideline of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics', vol. 16, e1, published 2014, https://doi.org/10.1038/gim.2014.128, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Heart and general care:** screen blood pressure from infancy, keep lipids normal, and screen for pulmonary hypertension by echocardiography from age 10 years, every 3 years. Avoid drugs that cause hypoglycaemia, and contact or competitive sports.
claims.locator: Kishnani PS, Austin SL, Abdenur JE, et al., Genetics in Medicine (ACMG), 'Diagnosis and management of glycogen storage disease type I: a practice guideline of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics', vol. 16, e1, published 2014, https://doi.org/10.1038/gim.2014.128, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Contraception and pregnancy:** avoid oestrogen contraceptives (adenoma risk) and, in GSD Ib, an IUD; plan pregnancies, stop ACE inhibitors, allopurinol and lipid-lowering drugs, and have a high-risk obstetric team manage them.
claims.locator: Kishnani PS, Austin SL, Abdenur JE, et al., Genetics in Medicine (ACMG), 'Diagnosis and management of glycogen storage disease type I: a practice guideline of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics', vol. 16, e1, published 2014, https://doi.org/10.1038/gim.2014.128, retrieved 2026-09-23
